$comment: HAND-TRANSCRIBED from each endpoint's PUBLIC model page (https://fal.ai/models/<id>). fal publishes no
machine-readable price anywhere — not in the Platform API, not in the OpenAPI document — so every rate here
is a human reading a sentence and writing down what it said, which is why each row carries the exact `quote`
it was read from, the `source` URL it was read at, and the date it was `verified`.
A curated endpoint with neither a rate nor an `unpriced` reason FAILS codegen. Silence about price is the one
thing this file may not say.
Row shape — either a rate:
unit      per_image | per_generation | per_megapixel | per_second | per_video_minute |
per_30_seconds | per_10_seconds | per_1000_characters | per_audio_minute |
per_input_audio_second | per_generated_audio_second | per_generated_audio_minute |
tiered | conditional | compute_second
usd       the scalar rate in that unit (absent for tiered/conditional — see `tiers`)
rounding  how fal rounds the billed quantity, verbatim from the page (e.g. megapixels round UP)
tierKey   what selects the tier (a wire field name, or prose when it is not one field)
tiers     [{ when, usd }] — the rates, each labelled by the condition that selects it
source / verified / quote
…or an explicit non-price:
unpriced  the REASON no rate can be stated, in prose
source / verified / quote
WHICH UNITS REACH `ModelCost` — deliberately only five, and only where the conversion is EXACT. The
target fields are the four `src/core/catalog-types.ts` publishes, per src/providers/HAND_CATALOGS.md:
per_image              → cost.perImage
per_second             → cost.perVideoSecond
per_1000_characters    → cost.perMillionCharacters (×1000 — exact, not a conversion factor)
per_audio_minute       → cost.perAudioMinute
per_input_audio_second → cost.perAudioMinute (×60 — exact, same rule as ×1000 above)
Every other unit emits NO `cost` on the generated row, and the rate survives as a provenance comment
above it instead. `ModelCost` is not widened in wave 1: a per-megapixel rate written into `perImage`
would be a number that is wrong for every image that is not exactly one megapixel, and `undefined`
beats a wrong number. Tiered and conditional rates land in the hand pricing table (kling precedent),
never here.
Wave 1d added five units, each because fal publishes a rate in it and none of the existing ten said the
same thing. Note which side of the microphone each one is on — that is what decides whether it can
reach `perAudioMinute`, whose own definition is "per minute of audio PROCESSED":
per_generation             a flat rate per request that is not an image — fal's "per audio" and
"per generation" wording at five music endpoints. `perImage` is an IMAGE
rate, so this reaches the catalog as a comment rather than as a number.
per_input_audio_second     a rate per second of INPUT audio (stt). ×60 to perAudioMinute, exactly.
per_generated_audio_second a rate per second of GENERATED audio (music). ModelCost has no such field.
per_generated_audio_minute the same, per minute — ElevenLabs Music, rounded up to the closest minute.
per_10_seconds             a per-block rate, the sibling of the per_30_seconds Lyria 2 already needed.
Wave 1e added six stretch rows and NO new unit, which was one of the three cheapness tests a stretch row
had to pass: three per_megapixel image rows, two per_second lipsync rows, and one `unpriced` — the
published microsoft/mai-image-2.5 page states no rate at all, and the internal route fal's own OpenAPI
documents shows only the unpopulated $0-per-compute-second template that wizper also shows.
Verified 2026-08-25 against the live pages.
Of the 146 rows here, 51 carry a unit ModelCost can express and therefore reach a generated catalog row;
the other 95 do not, which is the shape of fal's pricing rather than a gap in this file. The big classes:
conditional (48) needs a field the request often leaves at its default — at video that field is almost
always `resolution` or an audio switch, and fal quotes several of them per THOUSAND TOKENS of rendered
frames, which no request body counts; per_megapixel (18) needs the output's pixel count, and at upscale
that count is the INPUT file's area times the factor, which a submit body never carries because the
input arrives as a URL; tiered (7) needs a quantity the request does not state. All of them reach an
ESTIMATE through gen/pricing.gen.ts and src/providers/fal/pricing.ts, which computes what it can and
returns `undefined` — with a reason available from `falPriceNote` — for the rest. A plausible number
that is wrong is worse than no number: a caller who sees `costUSD` treats it as a budget.
